name: Adds numerators and adds denominators
description: Treats fraction addition like two separate whole-number sums, adding the tops together and the bottoms together.
signature: 1/4 + 2/3 = 3/7; 2/7 + 1/2 = 3/9; adds top numbers and bottom numbers of fractions; sum of fractions smaller than one of the fractions
probe: Is your answer bigger or smaller than the first fraction on its own? Should adding make it smaller?
remedy: Make the parts the same size first (common denominator), then count how many parts you have.

name: Common denominator without scaling numerators
description: Changes the denominators to a common one but leaves the numerators unchanged.
signature: 1/4 + 2/3 = 3/12; 1/5 + 3/10 = 4/10; uses common denominator but keeps original numerators; denominator changed numerator not multiplied
probe: When you changed quarters into twelfths, how many twelfths is one quarter?
remedy: Whatever you multiply the denominator by, multiply the numerator by the same number.

name: Believes multiplication always makes bigger
description: Assumes the product is always larger than the starting number, even when multiplying by a fraction or decimal less than 1.
signature: 15 x 0.2 is more than 15; multiplying by a decimal less than one gives a bigger number; product always greater; times makes bigger
probe: What is half of 15? Is taking 0.2 of something like taking a part of it?
remedy: Multiplying by a number less than 1 takes a part of the amount, so the result is smaller.

name: Cross-multiplies when multiplying fractions
description: Multiplies each numerator by the other fraction's denominator, mixing up the procedure with comparing or dividing fractions.
signature: 1/3 x 3/4 = 4/9; 2/5 x 1/3 = 6/5; cross multiplication used for fraction multiplication; multiplies numerator by other denominator
probe: If you take a third of three quarters, should the answer be more or less than three quarters?
remedy: Multiply straight across: top times top, bottom times bottom.

name: Flips the wrong fraction when dividing
description: Knows to use the reciprocal but inverts the first fraction (the dividend) instead of the divisor.
signature: 2/5 divided by 1/3 = 5/2 x 1/3 = 5/6; inverts the first fraction instead of the second; reciprocal of dividend; flips first fraction keep change flip wrong order
probe: Which fraction is the one you are dividing by? That is the one to flip.
remedy: Keep the first fraction, change divide to multiply, flip the second fraction.

name: Believes division always makes smaller
description: Assumes the quotient is always smaller than the starting number, even when dividing by a number less than 1.
signature: 15 divided by 0.2 is less than 15; dividing by a decimal gives a smaller answer; quotient always smaller; share makes smaller
probe: How many halves fit into 3 whole pizzas?
remedy: Dividing by a number less than 1 asks how many small parts fit, so the answer grows.

name: Thinks a longer decimal is larger
description: Compares decimals by the number of digits after the point, as if they were whole numbers.
signature: 0.65 is bigger than 0.7; 0.123 greater than 0.4; more decimal places means larger number; compares decimal digits as whole numbers 65 > 7
probe: How many tenths does each number have?
remedy: Compare place by place from the tenths; pad with zeros so both have the same length.

name: Misplaces the decimal point in a product
description: Counts the decimal places in only one factor, or keeps the decimal place of the inputs, when placing the point in the answer.
signature: 0.4 x 0.3 = 1.2; 1.6 x 0.2 = 3.2; keeps one decimal place in the product; decimal places not added; point placed using one factor
probe: Estimate first: is 0.4 x 0.3 bigger or smaller than 0.3?
remedy: Count the decimal places in both factors and give the answer that many places.

name: Two negatives make a positive when adding
description: Over-applies the multiplication sign rule to addition of negative numbers.
signature: -4 + (-6) = 10; adding two negative numbers gives a positive; minus plus minus is plus; sign rule from multiplication used in addition
probe: Start at -4 on the number line and move 6 more steps down. Where do you land?
remedy: Adding negatives moves further left on the number line; the sign rule is only for multiplying and dividing.

name: Subtracting a negative as subtracting a positive
description: Ignores the negative sign of the number being subtracted, treating a - (-b) as a - b.
signature: 9 - (-2) = 7; -8 - (-3) = -11; subtracting a negative number treated as normal subtraction; ignores double negative
probe: If you take away a debt of 2 rupees, are you richer or poorer?
remedy: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its opposite.

name: Works strictly left to right
description: Ignores operator precedence and evaluates expressions in reading order.
signature: 10 - 6 / 3 = 4/3; 5 + 3 x 4 = 32; evaluates from left to right ignoring BODMAS; addition before multiplication; ignores order of operations
probe: In BODMAS, which comes first: the addition or the multiplication?
remedy: Do multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

name: Combines unlike terms
description: Adds terms with different variables as if they were the same, often joining the letters together.
signature: 4p + 2q = 6pq; 3m + 5n = 8mn; adds unlike terms; joins different variables; collects letters into one term
probe: If p is pens and q is quills, what are 4 pens plus 2 quills?
remedy: Only like terms can be added; unlike terms stay separate.

name: Thinks a term added to itself is squared
description: Confuses repeated addition with repeated multiplication of a variable.
signature: y + y = y^2; m + m = m squared; adding same variable gives square; confuses doubling with squaring
probe: What is 5 + 5? And what is 5 x 5? Which one is y + y like?
remedy: y + y is two lots of y, so 2y; y x y is y squared.

name: Multiplies only the first term in the bracket
description: Applies the multiplier outside a bracket to the first term only.
signature: 4(y + 5) = 4y + 5; 2(m - 7) = 2m - 7; does not multiply second term in brackets; partial distribution
probe: Four bags each contain y apples and 5 mangoes. How many mangoes in total?
remedy: The number outside multiplies every term inside the bracket.

name: Sign error with a negative multiplier
description: Does not change the sign of every term when a minus sign or negative number multiplies a bracket.
signature: -(y - 7) = -y - 7; -3(m - 2) = -3m - 6; minus outside brackets only changes first sign; negative times negative inside bracket wrong
probe: What is -3 multiplied by -2?
remedy: A minus sign outside a bracket changes the sign of every term inside.

name: Moves a term across without changing the operation
description: Transposes a term to the other side of the equation but keeps its sign, breaking the balance.
signature: y + 4 = 10 so y = 14; 5y - 2 = 8 so 5y = 6; moves number across equals sign without changing sign; does not do inverse operation
probe: Substitute your answer back in. Does the left side equal the right side?
remedy: Undo each operation with its inverse on both sides of the balance.

name: Subtracts the coefficient instead of dividing
description: Undoes multiplication by a coefficient with subtraction.
signature: 5y = 20 so y = 15; 4m = 28 so m = 24; subtracts coefficient instead of dividing; wrong inverse operation for multiplication
probe: 5y means 5 times y. What undoes times 5?
remedy: Divide both sides by the coefficient.

name: Multiplies base by exponent
description: Reads a power as base times exponent.
signature: 3^4 = 12; 5 squared = 10; multiplies the base by the power; exponent as multiplication
probe: Write 3^4 out as a multiplication with only 3s. How many 3s?
remedy: The exponent counts how many times the base is multiplied by itself.

name: Multiplies exponents when multiplying powers
description: Multiplies the exponents instead of adding them when multiplying powers of the same base.
signature: b^4 x b^2 = b^8; m^3 x m^3 = m^9; multiplies indices instead of adding; power laws confused
probe: Write b^4 x b^2 out in full. How many b's are multiplied?
remedy: Same base multiplied: add the exponents.

name: Thinks anything to the power zero is zero
description: Assumes a zero exponent gives zero.
signature: 9^0 = 0; power of zero equals zero; zero exponent gives nothing
probe: What is 9^3 divided by 9^3? Now use the exponent rule for division.
remedy: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

name: Equal percentage up and down cancel out
description: Believes a percentage increase followed by the same percentage decrease returns to the original value.
signature: 200 increased by 20% then decreased by 20% is 200; percentage increase and decrease cancel; same percent up and down returns original
probe: The 20 percent decrease is 20 percent of which amount: 200 or 240?
remedy: The second percentage is taken of the new amount, so they do not cancel.

name: Uses the new value as the base for percentage change
description: Divides the change by the final value instead of the original value.
signature: 40 to 50 is a 20% increase; percentage change divided by new value; wrong base for percent change
probe: The change is measured against where you started. Where did you start?
remedy: Percentage change = change divided by original, times 100.

name: Squares each term separately
description: Believes (a + b) squared equals a squared + b squared, missing the 2ab term.
signature: (y + 5)^2 = y^2 + 25; (m + 2)^2 = m^2 + 4; squares each term in brackets; forgets middle term 2ab
probe: Try y = 1. Is (1 + 5) squared the same as 1 + 25?
remedy: (a + b) squared = (a + b)(a + b) = a squared + 2ab + b squared.

name: Treats a ratio part as a fraction of the other part
description: In a ratio a:b, takes a/b of the total instead of a/(a + b).
signature: 60 shared 1:4, smaller share is 1/4 of 60 = 15; ratio 1:4 means one quarter; uses a/b instead of a/(a+b)
probe: How many equal shares are there altogether in the ratio?
remedy: Add the ratio parts to find the total number of shares.
